one_liner: Vantel builds an AI platform for commercial insurance brokerages; its Y Combinator listing makes it worth tracking, but a reported seed round puts it past HTGF’s first-round window.

top_signals.signal: Vantel is listed in Y Combinator’s 2025–2026 European cohort.
The funding summary reports a $2 million seed round in March 2025 from Y Combinator, Inception Fund, Rebel Fund, and angel investors.

The lead ranks 13th of 63 today, with a model score 84.5 of 100 (at the top of the reference cohort). Fintech, deep tech, and YC participation flags lifted the score, as did flags for a founder CTO, a technical founder, study abroad, and attendance at a top university and a leading business school. The founder records confirm the CTO role but do not confirm the technical-founder flag, study abroad, or the school classifications.

team: Love Redin is founder and CEO; Ulme Wennberg is founder and CTO. Both list KTH Royal Institute of Technology. Wennberg also lists the Stockholm School of Economics and the University of Washington.
why_early: Unknown whether the reported March 2025 seed round was priced. The reported $2 million raise means Vantel is not a pre-first-round lead.
devils_advocate_risks: Established brokers may resist integrating AI into their workflows.
Adapting the platform to different insurance products and regional regulations could complicate scaling.
next_step: HTGF Industrial Tech team: confirm funding status before pursuing. Ask the founders: Was the March 2025 seed round a priced equity round?
